change.title: pr-80168-flat
change.description: feat(workflow_engine): Add in hook for producing occurrences from the stateful detector
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be constructed
findings.body:
The class now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler`, but its body is `pass`. `StatefulDetectorHandler` still declares abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and (new in this PR) `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:142-170). Instantiating the class therefore raises `TypeError`.

`MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` points at this class (line 27). `Detector.detector_handler` calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86), so a detector of type `metric_alert_fire` now raises inside `process_detectors` instead of returning no handler or `[]` as before. `MetricAlertFire` is registered automatically via `__init_subclass__` (src/sentry/issues/grouptype.py:163-165).

At head `process_detectors` has no production caller (only the re-export in src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/__init__.py:7), so this is latent. Fix in this PR: either restore the `DetectorHandler` base with the previous `evaluate` stub, or implement the four abstract members before switching the base class.

findings.title: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe expects an occurrence fingerprint for a different group key
findings.body: The expected occurrence is built for group key "val1" (lines 536-538), but the evaluated call uses group key "group_key" (line 548). `build_fingerprint` yields `f"{detector.id}:val1"` for the expected occurrence and `f"{detector.id}:group_key"` for the actual one. `IssueOccurrence` is a frozen dataclass with default equality (src/sentry/issues/issue_occurrence.py:66-67) and `fingerprint` is one of its fields, so the `== expected_result` assertion (lines 546-560) fails. Build the expected occurrence with "group_key" to match the call.

findings.title: Stale TODO above the now-stateful handler
findings.body: The comment on line 10 says the handler "will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction", but the class now extends `StatefulDetectorHandler`. Update or remove the comment together with the fix for the abstract-class problem above.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring of `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`", but the method now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (signature at lines 226-228, return at line 244). Update the docstring to say it returns a dict keyed by group key.

findings.title: Hook-call tests pass arbitrary values that the helper ignores
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` never uses its `value` argument, so the expected occurrences do not check the value the handler passes to the hook. Some tests pass a value different from the one evaluated: `test_results_on_change` evaluates `val1` at 100 (line 488) but builds the expected occurrence with 6 (line 490); `test_dedupe` evaluates 8 (line 508) and builds with 6 (line 510). A regression in which the handler passes the wrong value would not be caught. Either assert on the value or pass the evaluated value so the test reads correctly.

findings.title: TestProcessDetectors.setUp only calls super
findings.body: The `setUp` override at lines 125-126 only calls `super().setUp()` and does nothing else. Remove it, since it is inherited from `BaseDetectorHandlerTest`.

findings.title: Log for a missing grouptype always records group_type as "None"
findings.body: In the branch at lines 65-74, `group_type` is `None` by construction, so `str(group_type)` on line 69 always logs `"None"`. The PR already touches this function (`group_type = self.group_type`, line 64); the log should record the detector type, which is already in `detector_type` on line 71. This line predates the PR, so it is a cleanup, not a regression.

contracts.action: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now a StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty body, and Detector.detector_handler constructs it for metric_alert_fire detectors
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:114-129 (DetectorHandler base, which the class used before this PR)
contracts.before_after: Before: the class subclassed DetectorHandler, had no abstract members left unimplemented, could be constructed, and evaluate returned []. After: the class subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and inherits abstract counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values and build_occurrence_and_event_data, none implemented, so constructing it raises TypeError.
contracts.visible_effect: None at head: process_detectors has no production caller (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/__init__.py:7 only re-exports it).
contracts.failure_mode: Any caller of Detector.detector_handler for a metric_alert_fire detector gets TypeError from src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86 instead of a handler or None.

contracts.action: New Detector.group_type property, reused by detector_handler
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/issues/grouptype.py:104-107 (GroupTypeRegistry.get_by_slug, the lookup detector_handler did inline before)
contracts.before_after: Before: detector_handler looked up the slug inline. After: the same lookup runs through the property, which returns None for an unknown slug, and the existing None branch logs and returns None (lines 65-74). Behaviour is unchanged.
contracts.failure_mode: None: unknown slugs return None and are handled by the existing branch.

contracts.action: New call to build_occurrence_and_event_data for non-OK state transitions in evaluate_group_key_value
contracts.before_after: Before: the non-OK branch set result=None with a TODO for the occurrence hook, so no occurrence was produced. After: the hook builds an IssueOccurrence and event_data for each transition to a non-OK priority. The state update is enqueued before the hook runs (line 287).
contracts.visible_effect: process_detectors turns each non-None result into a Kafka message (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:60-62, 73-87). The producer requires event_data['event_id'] to match occurrence.event_id (src/sentry/issues/producer.py:100-101).
contracts.failure_mode: If the hook raises, the exception leaves evaluate before process_detectors reaches commit_state_updates (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:68), so this detector's dedupe, counter and state updates are not committed. Occurrences already produced for earlier results of the same detector are not rolled back. Nothing in the repository catches the exception.
contracts.open_question: How the Kafka occurrence is consumed and whether a produce failure after the hook is retried or lost. Only the producer side was read; the consumer was not.

contracts.action: process_detectors iterates handler results as a dict and drops the duplicate-group-key guard
contracts.before_after: Before: results were a list; duplicate result.group_key values were logged with logger.error and skipped. After: results are a dict, and the loop iterates .values(). The duplicate check and its error log are removed. StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate keys its dict by result.group_key (line 243), so duplicates cannot occur there.
contracts.failure_mode: None on the stateful path. A custom DetectorHandler that keys its dict by something other than group_key could produce duplicate group_keys without the error log, but no such handler exists at head.

summary: Reviewed the four files in this part. The main problem is in src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now extends StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty body, which leaves abstract members unimplemented, so constructing it raises TypeError (fix). It has no production caller of process_detectors at head, so it is latent. In the test file, TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds its expected occurrence for "val1" but evaluates "group_key". The fingerprints differ, so the test fails (fix). Other findings are stale docs, a test that ignores its value argument, a dead setUp, and a pre-existing log that always records None. Nothing was run, since the review is read-only. docs/adr/ does not exist in the snapshot, so there was no ADR to check against. The open contract is the Kafka consumer side of the new occurrence path, which is outside this part.
